agencies.name: 511NY
agencies.desc: 511 New York is the free, official one-stop, all-encompassing telephone and Web service offering information on transportation services and conditions throughout New York State. This information is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

agencies.name: Adirondack Park Agency
agencies.desc: The Adirondack Park Agency (APA) was created in 1971 by the New York State Legislature to develop long-range land use plans for both public and private lands within the boundary of the Park.

agencies.name: Authorities Budget Office
agencies.desc: The Authorities Budget Office makes public authorities more accountable and transparent, and acts in the public interest consistent with their intended purpose.

agencies.name: Battery Park City Authority
agencies.desc: Battery Park City Authority creates and maintains a balanced community of commercial, residential, retail, and park space within a 92-acre site on Manhattan's lower west side.

agencies.name: Board of Elections
agencies.desc: The State Board of Elections is responsible for administration and enforcement of all election laws, and regulates disclosure and limitations of campaign practices.

agencies.name: Bridge Authority
agencies.desc: The New York State Bridge Authority maintains and operates five bridges in the Hudson Valley, connecting counties to the east and west of the Hudson River.

agencies.name: Canal Corporation
agencies.desc: The New York State Canal system is a navigable 524-mile inland waterway that passes through 25 counties and close to 200 villages, hamlets, and towns in upstate New York.

agencies.name: Central Pine Barrens Joint Planning and Policy Commission
agencies.desc: The Central Pine Barrens Joint Planning and Policy Commission oversees the preservation and appropriate patterns of development in the 100,000+ acre region in Suffolk County.

agencies.name: City University of New York
agencies.desc: CUNY provides high-quality, accessible education for more than 269,000 degree-credit students and 247,000 continuing and professional education students at 24 campuses in NYC.

agencies.name: Commission of Correction
agencies.desc: The Commission of Correction is an oversight agency tasked with evaluating all state correctional facilities, county jails, local police lock-ups and secure centers operated by the State Office of Children and Family Services.

agencies.name: Commission on Ethics and Lobbying in Government (COELIG)
agencies.desc: COELIG was created to restore public trust in government by providing training and guidance on, and enforcement of, the State's ethics and lobbying laws, and promoting transparency in government through required disclosures.

agencies.name: Commission on Judicial Conduct
agencies.desc: The Commission on Judicial Conduct is responsible for investigating complaints of misconduct against judges of the state unified court system.

agencies.name: Commission on Prosecutorial Conduct
agencies.desc: The Commission on Prosecutorial Conduct (CPC) investigates prosecutorial conduct in New York State to strengthen oversight of New York's prosecutors and to hold them to the highest ethical standards.

agencies.name: Corcraft Products (Department of Correctional Services, Division of Industries)
agencies.desc: To employ inmates in substantive jobs that help teach a good work ethic and valuable work skills, to help offset the cost of incarceration, to help reduce disruption in the prison environment and to meet expectations of New York State's citizens.

agencies.name: Council on Children and Families Services
agencies.desc: Established by Chapter 757 of the laws of 1977, the Council provides a comprehensive, cross-systems perspective critical for solutions to interagency issues regarding services for children and families.

agencies.name: Council on Developmental Disabilities
agencies.desc: The NYSCDD enhances the lives of New Yorkers with Developmental Disabilities and their families through programs that promote self-advocacy, participation, and inclusion in all facets of community life.

agencies.name: Council on the Arts
agencies.desc: New York State Council on the Arts (NYSCA) is an agency of the Executive Branch of the New York State Government dedicated to preserving and expanding the rich and diverse cultural resources that are and will become the heritage of New York's people.

agencies.name: Department of Agriculture and Markets
agencies.desc: To promote New York agriculture and its high-quality and diverse products, foster agricultural environmental stewardship, and safeguard the State's food supply, land and livestock.

agencies.name: Department of Civil Service
agencies.desc: The Department of Civil Service is the State's principal human resources provider for the Executive Branch of Government.

agencies.name: Department of Corrections and Community Supervision
agencies.desc: The DOCCS enhances public safety by providing treatment services in safe facilities where needs are addressed in preparation for reentry, followed by supportive services under community supervision reducing recidivism.

agencies.name: Department of Education
agencies.desc: The Education Department's goals are to raise the knowledge, skill, and opportunity of all New Yorkers.

agencies.name: Department of Environmental Conservation
agencies.desc: The NYS Department of Environmental Conservation's (DEC) mission is to conserve, improve and protect New York's natural resources and environment.

agencies.name: Department of Financial Services
agencies.desc: The Department of Financial Services (DFS) regulates New York's financial service industry to guard against financial crises and to protect consumers and markets from fraud.

agencies.name: Department of Health
agencies.desc: To protect, improve and promote the health, productivity and well-being of all New Yorkers.

agencies.name: Department of Labor
agencies.desc: The mission of the New York State Department of Labor (DOL) is to protect workers, assist the unemployed and connect job seekers to jobs.

agencies.name: Department of Motor Vehicles
agencies.desc: DMV issues secure identity documents, delivers essential motor vehicle and driver related services, and administers motor vehicle laws to promote safety and protect consumers.

agencies.name: Department of Public Service
agencies.desc: The Commission sets rates and ensures New York's regulated utilities provide safe, reliable and adequate electric, gas, steam, telecommunications, water, and cable services.

agencies.name: Department of State
agencies.desc: The NY Department of State (DOS) provides many essential services to New Yorkers: Professional and Business Licensing, Incorporation, Consumer Protection and Local Government Services.

agencies.name: Department of Taxation and Finance
agencies.desc: To efficiently collect tax revenues in support of State services and programs while acting with integrity and fairness in the administration of the tax laws of New York State.

agencies.name: Department of Transportation
agencies.desc: It is the mission of the New York State Department of Transportation (DOT) to ensure our customers, those who live, work and travel in New York State, have a safe, efficient, balanced and environmentally sound transportation system.

agencies.name: Department of Veterans' Services
agencies.desc: NYS DVS advocates on behalf of New York's Veterans and their families, to ensure they receive benefits granted by law for service in the United States Armed Forces.

agencies.name: Division of Consumer Protection
agencies.desc: The mission of the Division of Consumer Protection is to protect, educate and represent consumers in an ever changing economy.

agencies.name: Division of Criminal Justice Services
agencies.desc: The New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services (DCJS) is a multi-function criminal justice support agency. Its mission is to enhance public safety by providing resources and services that inform decision making.

agencies.name: Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services
agencies.desc: The DHSES is dedicated to working closely with all levels of government, the private sector, and volunteer organizations to improve the readiness, response and recovery capabilities of communities throughout New York State.

agencies.name: Division of Human Rights
agencies.desc: The Division was created to enforce New York State's Human Rights Law, the first such law in the nation. Its mission is to ensure that every individual has an equal opportunity to participate fully in the economic, cultural and political life of the state.

agencies.name: Division of Military and Naval Affairs
agencies.desc: The New York National Guard provides fully capable military forces and facilities ready to execute global missions across unified air and land operations in support of our communities, state and nation.

agencies.name: Division of State Police
agencies.desc: To serve, protect and defend the people while preserving the rights and dignity of all.

agencies.name: Division of Tax Appeals and Tax Appeals Tribunal
agencies.desc: The Division of Tax Appeals is an independent and impartial body that resolves tax and licensing disputes, and is headed by the Tax Appeals Tribunal.

agencies.name: Division of the Budget
agencies.desc: DOB assists the governor in preparing the Executive Budget, offers fiscal policy advice to the governor's office, and administers and monitors expenditures.

agencies.name: Dormitory Authority
agencies.desc: DASNY is New York State's public finance and construction authority. DASNY is authorized to finance, design, construct or rehabilitate facilities for certain public and private not-for-profit entities.

agencies.name: Empire State Development
agencies.desc: ESD works to attract new businesses to the state and support the growth of existing firms by means of financial incentives, real estate development, marketing, and small business services.

agencies.name: Energy Research and Development Authority
agencies.desc: NYSERDA offers objective information and analysis, innovative programs, technical expertise and funding to help New Yorkers increase energy efficiency and use renewable energy.

agencies.name: Environmental Facilities Corporation
agencies.desc: EFC's environmental initiatives extend financial and technical assistance to municipalities, non-profits and small businesses, ensuring they meet water and air quality regulations.

agencies.name: Financial Control Board
agencies.desc: The New York State Financial Control Board oversees the financial management of the New York City government and certain related public authorities.

agencies.name: Gaming Commission
agencies.desc: The Gaming Commission regulates legal gambling in New York, including horse racing, Indian gaming, the state lottery (including video lottery terminals), commercial casinos, and charitable gaming.

agencies.name: Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
agencies.desc: The NYS Geospatial Advisory Council coordinates, promotes and facilitates the development, effective use, and sharing of geographic information.

agencies.name: Governor's Traffic Safety Committee
agencies.desc: Governor's Traffic Safety Committee awards Federal grant funds to local, state and nonprofit agencies to improve highway safety and reduce deaths and injuries due to crashes.

agencies.name: Higher Education Services Corporation
agencies.desc: The Higher Education Services Corporation (HESC) is New York State's higher education student financial aid agency. HESC's mission: We help people pay for college.

agencies.name: Homes and Community Renewal
agencies.desc: New York State Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) consists of all the State's major housing and community renewal agencies, including the Affordable Housing Corporation, the Division of Housing and Community Renewal, the Housing Finance Agency and the State of New York Mortgage Agency.

agencies.name: Housing Finance Agency/State of NY Mortgage Agency (SONYMA)
agencies.desc: SONYMA provides mortgage financing to assist low and moderate income first-time homebuyers who meet specific eligibility criteria, in the purchase of 1-4 unit residences.

agencies.name: Hudson River Park Trust
agencies.desc: Hudson River Park Trust is charged with the design, construction and operation of the 5-mile Hudson River Park, the largest open space project in Manhattan since Central Park.

agencies.name: Hudson River Valley Greenway
agencies.desc: The Hudson River Valley Greenway facilitates the development of a regional strategy for preserving natural resources while encouraging economic development.

agencies.name: Jacob K. Javits Convention Center
agencies.desc: The Jacob K. Javits Convention Center of New York is the busiest convention center in the United States, hosting the world's leading conventions, trade shows and special events.

agencies.name: Justice Center for the Protection of People with Special Needs
agencies.desc: The NYS Justice Center for the Protection of People with Special Needs is dedicated to supporting and protecting people with special needs and disabilities.

agencies.name: Liquidation Bureau
agencies.desc: The New York Liquidation Bureau carries out the duties of the Superintendent of Financial Services in the capacity of receiver of impaired or insolvent insurance companies.

agencies.name: Liquor Authority, Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control
agencies.desc: The Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control operates under the direction of the State Liquor Authority, a three-member Board consisting of a Chairperson, who acts as the agency administrator, and two Commissioners, appointed by the Governor.

agencies.name: Metropolitan Transportation Authority
agencies.desc: MTA operating agencies include New York City Transit, Long Island Rail Road, Metro-North Railroad, Staten Island Railroad, MTA Bridges and Tunnels, MTA Capital Construction, and MTA Bus.

agencies.name: MTA Inspector General
agencies.desc: The MTA preserves and enhances the quality of life and economic health of the region it serves through the cost-efficient provision of safe, on-time, reliable and clean transportation services.

agencies.name: New York Assembly
agencies.desc: The New York State Assembly is the lower house of the State Legislature. It is composed of 150 members, each representing a district with an average population of 128,652.

agencies.name: New York State Insurance Fund
agencies.desc: NYSIF provides workers' compensation and disability benefits insurance to businesses operating in New York State, covering eligible workers injured on and off the job.

agencies.name: New York State Law Revision Commission
agencies.desc: The Commission examines State laws and current judicial decisions for the purpose of discovering defects and anachronisms in the law and recommending needed reforms.

agencies.name: New York State Senate
agencies.desc: The New York State Senate is the upper house in the State Legislature. It currently has 63 members each elected to two-year terms without term limits.

agencies.name: NYC 311
agencies.desc: 311 is New York City's main source of government information and non-emergency services. Whether you are a resident, a business owner, or a visitor, help is just a click, text or call away.

agencies.name: Office for New Americans
agencies.desc: The Office for New Americans (ONA) assists newcomers in New York State who are eager to contribute to our economy and become part of the family of New York.

agencies.name: Office for People With Developmental Disabilities
agencies.desc: The Office for People with Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD) assists people with developmental disabilities and their families in gaining access to high-quality services and supports tailored to each person's unique needs.

agencies.name: Office for the Aging
agencies.desc: The mission of the New York State Office for the Aging (NYSOFA) is to help older New Yorkers be as independent as possible for as long as possible through advocacy, development and delivery of person-centered, consumer-oriented, and cost-effective policies, programs and services.

agencies.name: Office for the Prevention of Domestic Violence
agencies.desc: The Office for the Prevention of Domestic Violence (OPDV) is the country's only executive level state agency dedicated to the issue of domestic violence.

agencies.name: Office of Addiction Services and Supports
agencies.desc: OASAS oversees one of the nation's largest addiction services systems with nearly 1,600 prevention, treatment and recovery programs. OASAS chemical dependence treatment programs assist about 100,000 people a day.

agencies.name: Office of Cannabis Management
agencies.desc: The Marijuana Regulation and Taxation Act creates a first in the nation comprehensive regulatory structure to oversee the licensure, cultivation, production, distribution, sale and taxation of medical, adult-use and cannabinoid hemp within New York State.

agencies.name: Office of Children and Family Services
agencies.desc: The Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS) serves New York's public by promoting the safety and well-being of our children and families.

agencies.name: Office of Counter Terrorism
agencies.desc: OCT works closely with the New York State Police and other law enforcement and public safety agencies in the fight against terrorism.

agencies.name: Office of Emergency Management
agencies.desc: Office of Emergency Management (OEM) coordinates the activities of all State agencies to protect New York's communities, the State's economic well-being, and the environment from natural and man-made disasters and emergencies.

agencies.name: Office of Employee Relations
agencies.desc: OER represents the Governor in negotiating collective bargaining agreements. OER also administers a variety of programs for the State workforce.

agencies.name: Office of Fire Prevention and Control
agencies.desc: OFPC advances public safety through firefighter training, education, fire prevention, investigative, special operations and technical rescue programs.

agencies.name: Office of General Services
agencies.desc: OGS streamlines government by managing real estate, business services, design, construction, and more for agencies. Its procurement services help the state, towns and others buy smarter.

agencies.name: Office of Information Technology Services
agencies.desc: ITS provides centralized IT services to the State and its governmental entities. ITS also sets statewide technology policy for all state government agencies.

agencies.name: Office of Interoperable and Emergency Communications (OIEC)
agencies.desc: Directs interoperable and emergency communications, and implementation of all aspects of interoperable and emergency communications including land and mobile radio communications.

agencies.name: Office of Mental Health
agencies.desc: The New York State Office of Mental Health (OMH) promotes the mental health and well-being of all New Yorkers. Its mission is to facilitate recovery for young to older adults receiving treatment for serious mental illness.

agencies.name: Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation
agencies.desc: The Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (OPRHP) is responsible for the operation and stewardship of the state parks system, as well as advancing a statewide parks, historic preservation, recreational, and open space mission.

agencies.name: Office of State Comptroller
agencies.desc: New York State Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli is the State's chief fiscal officer who ensures that State and local governments use taxpayer money effectively and efficiently to promote the common good.

agencies.name: Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance
agencies.desc: OTDA helps vulnerable New Yorkers meet their essential needs and advance economically by providing opportunities for stable employment, housing, and nutrition.

agencies.name: Office of the Governor
agencies.desc: Governor Kathy Hochul is the 57th and first female Governor of New York State.

agencies.name: Office of the Medicaid Inspector General
agencies.desc: Its mission is to enhance the integrity of the New York State Medicaid program by preventing and detecting fraudulent, abusive, and wasteful practices within the Medicaid program.

agencies.name: Office of Victim Services
agencies.desc: The Office of Victim Services provides a safety net for individuals and their families who have been victimized through no fault of their own and have no other means of assistance. OVS also funds programs providing direct services to crime victims.

agencies.name: Offices of the Inspector General
agencies.desc: The Inspector General's Offices ensure that NYS government, its employees and those working with the state meet high standards of honesty, accountability, and efficiency.

agencies.name: Olympic Regional Development Authority
agencies.desc: ORDA was originally created by the State of New York to manage the facilities used during the 1980 Olympic Winter Games at Lake Placid. Today, ORDA operates Whiteface Mountain ski area, Gore Mountain ski area and Belleayre Mountain, as well as the Olympic venues.

agencies.name: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
agencies.desc: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey builds, operates, and maintains many of the most important transportation and infrastructure assets in the country.

agencies.name: Power Authority
agencies.desc: The NY Power Authority (NYPA) is the nation's largest state power organization, serving government, not-for-profit, and business customers.

agencies.name: Roosevelt Island Operating Corporation of the State of New York (RIOC)
agencies.desc: RIOC is a public-benefit corporation responsible for developing Roosevelt Island, a small strip of land in the East River, part of the borough of Manhattan.

agencies.name: South Shore Estuary Council
agencies.desc: The South Shore Estuary Reserve was formed by the State Legislature at the urging of Long Islanders concerned with the long-term health of the Estuary.

agencies.name: State Employees Federated Appeal (SEFA)
agencies.desc: SEFA is a charitable solicitation of New York state employees, where they contribute to charitable organizations through payroll deduction.

agencies.name: State University Construction Fund
agencies.desc: The Fund provides the means for the construction of academic buildings, dormitories and other facilities for the State-operated institutions.

agencies.name: State University of New York (SUNY)
agencies.desc: The State University of New York is the largest comprehensive university system in the United States, educating nearly 460,000 students on 64 college and university campuses and online through Open SUNY.

agencies.name: Teachers' Retirement System
agencies.desc: NYSTRS administers a defined benefit plan that provides retirement, disability and death benefits to eligible New York State public school teachers and administrators.

agencies.name: Thruway Authority
agencies.desc: The New York State Thruway is one of the longest toll roads in the nation and is a vital commercial link for New York's largest cities and for the entire Northeast.

agencies.name: Waterfront Commission
agencies.desc: The New York Waterfront Commission investigates and prevents crime and unfair hiring practices in the Port of New York to protect workers, businesses, and the public.

agencies.name: Workers Compensation Board
agencies.desc: The New York State Workers' Compensation Board protects the rights of employees and employers by ensuring the proper delivery of benefits to those who are injured or ill, and by promoting compliance with the law.
